_comment: Photograph-licensing triage for the 51 person cards. class A = a verifiably free photograph exists and ships unmodified as a file in src/assets/ with a credits-block entry in src/template.html. class B = no free photograph; the card gets an authored portrait, and NO drawing may be traced or derived from any BY-SA source photo. class C = no identifiable subject; the card gets the no-known-likeness mark. Public-domain and CC0 entries below are the only ones a drawing may safely be traced from. Licences were read off each file's own description page (Commons extmetadata + raw licence template), not off the Wikipedia article that uses the file. Nothing has been downloaded; a later pass fetches.

p0c01.name: Henry A. Murray
p0c01.reason: Harvard personality psychologist, OSS Station S, 1943. The only portrait photograph in circulation is en-wiki File:Henry Murray.jpg, tagged {{Non-free biog-pic}} fair use, sourced to the Harvard University Archives. Commons holds two decoys: File:Henry Murray (1893-1988).jpg is a photograph of a Franklin Chenault Watkins oil portrait (Watkins d. 1972, painting still in copyright, the CC BY-SA 4.0 tag is the uploader licensing someone else's painting) and File:A group of Chinese and American psychologists during WWII.jpg is a 1945 thirteen-person group shot tagged {{PD-China}} only, with no US copyright tag and no evidence of pre-1978 publication (its cited source is a 2015 book). Neither survives scrutiny.

p0c02.name: Max Levchin
p0c02.reason: PayPal CTO. TechCrunch's Flickr stream is blanket CC BY 2.0 and this frame is FlickreviewR-passed on Commons.
p0c02.attribution: Max Levchin at TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2013, photograph by TechCrunch, CC BY 2.0.

p1c01.name: Bob Braden
p1c01.reason: USC/ISI, RFC 1644. Carl Malamud's 'Exploring the Internet' photographs are released CC BY 2.0; this is the image en-wiki uses on the Bob Braden article.
p1c01.attribution: Bob Braden in 1996, photograph by Carl Malamud for 'Exploring the Internet', CC BY 2.0.

p1c02.name: Bruce Jay Nelson
p1c02.reason: Xerox PARC, RPC thesis 1981; died 1999. The single Commons candidate, File:BruceJayNelson.JPG, carries {{self|cc-by-3.0}} while its own description reads 'Photo by Richard James, July 1996'. The uploader is not the photographer, so the self-licence is void on the face of the page and there is no VRT ticket. Cannot verify, therefore B.

p1c03.name: Pat Selinger
p1c03.reason: IBM San Jose, System R optimiser, 1979. Photographed at Michael Stonebraker's 70th-birthday celebration, 2014; the stonebraker70.com photo set is released CC BY 4.0.
p1c03.attribution: Pat Selinger at Michael Stonebraker's 70th birthday celebration, 2014, photograph by Jacek Ambroziak and Sam Madden, CC BY 4.0.

p1c04.name: The Terremark manager
p1c04.reason: Unnamed. The card's subject is a role, not a person: the Terremark hosting manager on the HealthCare.gov launch call of 26 September 2013. No name appears in the CMS or OIG record, so there is nothing to photograph and nothing to draw.

p1c05.name: Gene Amdahl
p1c05.reason: IBM, Amdahl's law, 1967. Photographed at a University of Wisconsin-Madison CS event in San Jose, 2008; uploader is the photographer, licence CC BY 3.0. Several further CC BY-SA 4.0 shots by Arnamdbak exist as alternates.
p1c05.attribution: Gene Myron Amdahl, 13 March 2008, photograph by Perry Kivolowitz, CC BY 3.0.

p1c06.name: J. S. Liptay
p1c06.reason: IBM Systems Journal author, 1968, Model 85 cache. No file on Wikimedia Commons, no Wikidata item, no en-wiki article. IBM Systems Journal of that era printed author biographies with headshots, but those are IBM copyright and have never been released; the IBM Archives holdings are all rights reserved.

p1c07.name: Mark Bergsma
p1c07.reason: Wikimedia Foundation network/ops, 2007. WMF staff portrait by Lane Hartwell, released CC BY-SA 3.0. Note the page carries a personality-rights advisory: it is a staff portrait, use is editorial and non-endorsing here, which is fine, but do not use it decoratively on the sell page.
p1c07.attribution: Mark Bergsma, June 2008, photograph by Lane Hartwell on behalf of the Wikimedia Foundation, CC BY-SA 3.0.

p1c08.name: Roger W. Ferguson, Jr.
p1c08.reason: Fed Governor and Vice Chairman on 11 September 2001. Official Board of Governors portrait, released via the Board's Flickr and tagged {{PD-USGov-Federal Reserve}}, FlickreviewR-passed as 'United States Government Work'. Public domain, so it may also be traced if a drawing is preferred later.
p1c08.attribution: Vice Chairman Roger W. Ferguson Jr., Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Public domain (work of the US federal government).

p1c09.name: Chuanhui
p1c09.reason: Taobao engineer writing as the author of NOSQL Notes, 22 April 2011; the handle maps to a real, identifiable Alibaba/OceanBase engineer. No Commons file, no Wikidata item. Such photographs as exist are Alibaba conference and press material, all rights reserved.

p1c10.name: David K. Gifford
p1c10.reason: Weighted voting for replicated data, SOSP 1979; later MIT CSAIL. No Commons file, no en-wiki article, no Wikidata image. MIT faculty and CSAIL portraits are all rights reserved.

p1c11.name: John Wilby
p1c11.reason: Chief Executive, London Ambulance Service, resigned 28 October 1992. No Commons file, no en-wiki article. Contemporary coverage carried press-agency photographs (PA/Getty), all rights reserved.

p1c12.name: G. Ratta
p1c12.reason: Named only as chief editor on the title page of ATM Forum UNI 3.1 (Bellcore, 1994). No biography, no obituary, no photograph, no Wikidata item, nothing in Commons or the ATM Forum record. Identifiable as a name, but no documented appearance to draw from.

p1c13.name: E. F. Codd
p1c13.reason: The only photograph in circulation is en-wiki File:Edgar F Codd.jpg, whose own page says 'Seems to be copyright IBM. Claiming fair use' under {{Non-free fair use in|Edgar F. Codd}}, sourced to an IBM Research obituary page. Commons has nothing. Textbook case of an article photo that is not free.

p1c14.name: Richard M. Smith
p1c14.reason: Phar Lap Software, Cambridge MA; traced the Melissa virus via the Office GUID in 1999. En-wiki article carries no image; no Commons file, no Wikidata image. 1999 news coverage used agency photographs, all rights reserved.

p2c01.name: Peter W. Allsopp
p2c01.reason: Bank of England, chaired the BIS/CPSS steering group on settlement risk in foreign exchange transactions, 1996. No Commons file, no en-wiki article. BIS and Bank of England photographs are all rights reserved.

p2c02.name: Seema Misra
p2c02.reason: West Byfleet subpostmistress, convicted 2010, conviction quashed 2021. Heavily photographed, but every frame is PA Media, Reuters or Getty; the en-wiki coverage of the Post Office scandal uses no free portrait of her and Commons has none.

p2c03.name: John Owen, passed-fireman
p2c03.reason: Cambrian Railways footplate crew killed in the Abermule collision, 26 January 1921. Named in Colonel Pringle's Ministry of Transport report and nowhere else. Commons holds photographs of Abermule station and the tablet-exchange layout but no likeness of any crew member. No known likeness.

p2c04.name: Imine, Molli, Oster and Rusinowitch
p2c04.reason: ECOO/CASSIS teams at LORIA, Nancy, 2003, on operational-transformation correctness. Searched Commons for Abdessamad Imine, Pascal Molli, Gerald Oster and Michael Rusinowitch: nothing for any of the four. INRIA and LORIA staff photographs are all rights reserved. Four authored portraits, or one composite.

p2c05.name: Larry Seese
p2c05.reason: AT&T director of technology development, spokesman on the 15 January 1990 network collapse. No Commons file, no en-wiki article. 1990 wire-service photographs only, all rights reserved.

p2c06.name: CCP Veritas
p2c06.reason: A CCP Games dev-blog handle for the Team Gridlock performance engineer who wrote the Time Dilation posts. CCP has never publicly attached a name or a face to it. No identifiable subject.

p2c07.name: John Nagle
p2c07.reason: Ford Aerospace, RFC 896, 1984. Searched Commons for 'John Nagle' and 'Nagle': only an unrelated New Jersey house, Civil War enlistment cards and an unrelated 2026 convention photo. No free portrait of the RFC 896 author exists.

p2c08.name: Craig Faust
p2c08.reason: TMI-2 control room operator. Appears, named, in the Kemeny Commission report photograph of the operators testifying: 'Seated (l to r) are Ernest Blake, legal counsel to Met Ed, and operators Fred Scheimann, William Zewe, Edward Frederick, and Craig Faust.' A US Presidential Commission report, so {{PD-USGov}}. Group shot, and public domain, so it may be cropped, halftoned or traced freely.
p2c08.attribution: TMI-2 control room operators testifying before the Commission, October 1979. Report of the President's Commission on the Accident at Three Mile Island, p. 95. Public domain (work of the US federal government).

p2c09.name: Masumi Yamada
p2c09.reason: Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University, on earthquake early-warning false alarms. No Commons file, no en-wiki article, no Wikidata image. University and JMA photographs are all rights reserved.

p2c10.name: M. Douglas McIlroy
p2c10.reason: Bell Labs, the pipe and the spell-checker. Flickr photograph by Denise Panyik-Dale, CC BY 2.0, FlickreviewR-passed; this is the image en-wiki uses.
p2c10.attribution: Douglas McIlroy in 2011, photograph by Denise Panyik-Dale, CC BY 2.0.

p2c11.name: Mark Steward
p2c11.reason: FCA Executive Director of Enforcement and Market Oversight, on the TSB migration, 2022. No Commons file (a search returns only the tomb of a sixteenth-century Sir Mark Steward), no Wikidata image. FCA portraits are all rights reserved.

p3c01.name: F. G. Foster
p3c01.reason: Gordon Foster, who devised the nine-digit Standard Book Number for W.H. Smith in 1965-67; later Trinity College Dublin, died 2010. No en-wiki article, no Commons file, no Wikidata image. TCD and obituary photographs are all rights reserved.

p3c02.name: Grover, King and Kushler
p3c02.reason: Dale Grover, Martin King and Cliff Kushler, the T9 patent (US application 08/507,756, 1995). Kushler has an en-wiki article with no photograph and a Wikidata item with no P18; Grover and King have neither. Nothing on Commons for any of the three. Company and press-kit photographs only.

p3c03.name: Liz Kowalczyk
p3c03.reason: Boston Globe health reporter, the 2011 alarm-fatigue investigation. No Commons file, no Wikidata item. Her Globe staff photograph is Boston Globe Media property, all rights reserved.

p3c04.name: Craig Partridge
p3c04.reason: CSNET CIC and BBN, RFC 1035 mail routing. Internet Hall of Fame induction video, 2017, published on the Internet Society's 'Imagining the Internet' YouTube channel under YouTube's standard CC BY 3.0 option; the Commons still frame carries {{Cc-by-3.0}} and passed licence review.
p3c04.attribution: Craig Partridge, 2017 Internet Hall of Fame inductee, Imagining the Internet / Internet Society, CC BY 3.0.

p3c05.name: Fu Wen (付稳)
p3c05.reason: Technical lead on the Weibo hybrid-cloud DCP project, 2017; a real and identifiable engineer who has presented at Chinese architecture conferences. No Commons file, no Wikidata item. Conference and InfoQ speaker headshots are all rights reserved.

p3c06.name: Robert Richard Torrens
p3c06.reason: Colony of South Australia, 1858. Glass-negative portrait held by the History Trust of South Australia and released CC0. Public-domain-equivalent, so it may also be traced. A second option, File:Robert Richard Torrens.jpg (c. 1880, unidentified photographer), is plain public domain by age.
p3c06.attribution: Sir Robert Richard Torrens, c. 1855, State Government Photographer, collection of the History Trust of South Australia, CC0 1.0.

p3c07.name: Steve Beckhardt
p3c07.reason: Iris Associates, the fourth engineer on Notes, c. 1985. No Commons file, no en-wiki article, no Wikidata item. Lotus and IBM photographs are all rights reserved.

p3c08.name: A. K. Manocha and Sanjaya Das
p3c08.reason: Exactly the event on the card: the Press Information Bureau photographed the IRCTC/CRIS joint press conference in New Delhi on 19 January 2016, with both men named in the caption. Released under GODL-India, which permits reproduction and adaptation with attribution. Note the licence is not CC: the credits block must name GODL-India specifically, and if the image is halftoned the adaptation stays under GODL-India's attribution terms.
p3c08.attribution: The CMD, IRCTC, Dr A. K. Manocha, and the MD, CRIS, Shri Sanjaya Das, at a combined press conference in New Delhi, 19 January 2016. Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Railways, Government of India (PIB ID 75804), GODL-India.

p3c09.name: Martijn Koster
p3c09.reason: Nexor, robots.txt, 1994. En-wiki article carries no image; Wikidata item Q6774756 has no P18; Commons has nothing. No free photograph exists.

p3c10.name: Hideo Tomioka
p3c10.reason: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, Japan, 2012, on the DoCoMo control-plane outages. No Commons file, no en-wiki article. Japanese government press photography is not blanket-free and MIC material is all rights reserved.

p3c11.name: Tracey McDermott
p3c11.reason: FCA director of enforcement and financial crime, 2014, on the RBS CA-7 batch failure. Wikidata item Q22279127 has no P18; nothing on Commons. FCA and press photographs only, all rights reserved.

p3c12.name: Graham Cormode and S. Muthukrishnan
p3c12.reason: Count-Min sketch, DIMACS/Rutgers and AT&T Research, 2003. Neither has a Commons file; the en-wiki article on S. Muthukrishnan carries no image and there is no en-wiki article for Cormode with a photograph. University and lab portraits are all rights reserved.

p3c13.name: George W. Ivie
p3c13.reason: Executive Director and CEO of the Media Rating Council, 2021. No Commons file (a search returns only an unrelated George Ivie Mackesy, d. 1917), no Wikidata image. MRC and trade-press photographs are all rights reserved.

p3c14.name: E. Gerald Corrigan
p3c14.reason: President of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York during the 1985 Bank of New York overdraft. The usable file is already cropped to him out of a Board of Governors Flickr group portrait of current and former Minneapolis Fed presidents, tagged {{PD-USGov-Federal Reserve}}. Public domain, so free to trace as well as to ship. The photograph is late-career, not 1985.
p3c14.attribution: E. Gerald Corrigan, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Public domain (work of the US federal government).

p3c15.name: Lars and Jens Rasmussen
p3c15.reason: Both brothers have free photographs, from two different files and two different photographers, so the card needs two images or a two-up crop. Lars: Google Developer Day Australia, 2007, CC BY-SA 2.0. Jens: File:JensEilstrupRasmussen.jpg, own work by uploader ZaphodsCatwalk, CC BY-SA 3.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:JensEilstrupRasmussen.jpg. Both are BY-SA: ship unmodified, do not trace, and if either is halftoned the halftone itself ships BY-SA.
p3c15.attribution: Lars Rasmussen at Google Developer Day Australia, Australian Technology Park, 31 May 2007, photograph by Charlie Brewer, CC BY-SA 2.0. Jens Eilstrup Rasmussen, photograph by Wikimedia Commons user ZaphodsCatwalk, CC BY-SA 3.0.

p3c16.name: Brad Fitzpatrick
p3c16.reason: The cleanest case in the cast: Fitzpatrick published the file himself at bradfitz.com/public-domain/ and it is tagged public domain on Commons, author Brad Fitzpatrick. Free to crop, halftone or trace.
p3c16.attribution: Brad Fitzpatrick, photograph released into the public domain by Brad Fitzpatrick (bradfitz.com/public-domain/).

p3c17.name: Mendel Rosenblum and John Ousterhout
p3c17.reason: Rosenblum has a clean CC BY-SA 3.0 photograph (VMworld Europe 2008, own work by uploader Janex) and that is the file recorded below. Ousterhout's only free image is File:Ouster face.png, the headshot shipped with the Tcl/Tk source distribution, tagged {{Tcl/Tk}} on Commons: a BSD-style permissive licence that allows redistribution and modification provided the copyright notice is kept, author John Ousterhout, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ouster_face.png. That is a free licence but not a CC one, so if the credits block should carry only CC and PD terms, draw Ousterhout and photograph Rosenblum.
p3c17.attribution: Mendel Rosenblum at VMworld Europe 2008, photograph by Wikimedia Commons user Janex, CC BY-SA 3.0. John Ousterhout, photograph shipped with the Tcl/Tk distribution, © John Ousterhout, Tcl/Tk licence (BSD-style).

p3c18.name: Mike Unum
p3c18.reason: GE Energy manager of commercial solutions, the XA/21 race-condition disclosure after the 2003 blackout. No Commons file, no Wikidata item. GE corporate photography and trade-press headshots only, all rights reserved.

p3c19.name: Roberto Busa
p3c19.reason: Index Thomisticus, 1949. Photographed at Gallarate in 2006 by Antonio G Colombo, who released it CC0 on Commons (the file was also earlier on it-wiki under GFDL 1.2; the CC0 dedication is the operative one). CC0, so it may be halftoned or traced. Ideal frame too: Busa in front of the Index Thomisticus itself.
p3c19.attribution: Father Roberto Busa SJ with the Index Thomisticus, Gallarate, 19 September 2006, photograph by Antonio G Colombo, CC0 1.0.

p3c20.name: Cheng Huang
p3c20.reason: Microsoft Research, Local Reconstruction Codes for Windows Azure Storage, 2012. The en-wiki page 'Cheng Huang' carries no image and Commons has nothing for him. Microsoft Research portraits are all rights reserved.

p3c21.name: Drew Major
p3c21.reason: Chairman of Move Networks, 2007; earlier Novell chief scientist. Commons has File:2005 dmajor bw.jpg tagged {{PD-author}} with the note 'Drew Major Press Photo Released into PD to the Utah Technology Council and online sites'. That is a third-party assertion about a press photo, with no named photographer and no VRT ticket: exactly the press-kit pattern the brief flags. Unverifiable, therefore B.

p3c22.name: Koichiro Miyahara
p3c22.reason: President of the Tokyo Stock Exchange who resigned after the 1 October 2020 arrowhead outage. Commons has File:KoichiroMiyahara.jpg, but it is a 1920 photograph of an unrelated Japanese writer of the same name. No free photograph of the TSE president exists; Reuters and Kyodo hold the 2020 press-conference frames.

p3c23.name: Gyeong-In Yu
p3c23.reason: Orca continuous batching, OSDI 2022; Seoul National University and FriendliAI. No Commons file, no Wikidata item, no free conference photography. Company and conference headshots are all rights reserved.

p3c24.name: Weber, Schek and Blott
p3c24.reason: One of the three is covered. Hans-Jorg Schek has an ETH-Bibliothek portrait (2005) released CC BY-SA 4.0 through the ETH/Wikimedia CH cooperation; the page carries a personality-rights advisory. Roger Weber and Stephen Blott have nothing on Commons and no free photograph anywhere, so they need authored portraits: the card is a photograph-plus-two-drawings unless all three are drawn for consistency.
p3c24.attribution: Hans-Jorg Schek, 2005, photographer unknown, ETH-Bibliothek Zurich, Bildarchiv, CC BY-SA 4.0.
